title: What happens in read()?
question: A program reads 64 bytes of a file. Which parts of the kernel does that go through? (Here the file is in memory: no disk.)
text: Call 2, [read(fd, [64], 64)](2): [ksys_read](2:ksys_read) The syscall: the fd turns into the open file (a struct file), and the position to read at. [vfs_read](2:vfs_read) The VFS, the same for every file system: is the file open for reading, is the range sane? Then the file system's own read. [filemap_read](2:filemap_read) The page cache: a file's data lives in memory pages. Find the page at the position, and copy from it to the program. (In ramfs, the pages are all the file is.)
